standard.title: Segment and blend phonemes
standard.description: segment sentences into individual words; orally blend and segment single-syllable spoken words; isolate, blend and manipulate phonemes in single-syllable words (phonological awareness)
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise phonemes (AC9EFLY09). They have not yet been explicitly taught to blend phonemes into words, segment words into phonemes, or manipulate individual phonemes by substitution, addition or deletion.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can blend phonemes into words, segment single-syllable words into phonemes, and manipulate phonemes by addition, deletion and substitution — demonstrating secure phoneme-level awareness across a range of single-syllable word types.

nodes.label: Sentences are strings of words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can segment a spoken sentence into its individual words — identifying where word boundaries fall.
nodes.minimum_width: Segment a spoken sentence of three to four words into individual words by clapping or tapping.
nodes.typical_width: Segment sentences into individual words; understand that words are the units within sentences; count words in short spoken sentences.
wider: Apply word segmentation to sentences of varying length — including sentences with contractions and function words
Connect spoken word segmentation to written word spaces — matching oral and print word boundaries
success_criteria: Student correctly segments a spoken sentence into its individual words.
Student can count the number of words in a spoken sentence.

nodes.label: Blending: sounds into words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can blend a sequence of separately spoken phonemes into a recognisable word.
nodes.minimum_width: Blend three phonemes into a CVC word when given the sounds separately (e.g. /l/-/i/-/p/ → 'lip').
nodes.typical_width: Blend phonemes of single-syllable spoken words — including CVC, CVCC and CCVC patterns; produce the target word correctly from the phoneme sequence.
wider: Blend phoneme sequences across a wide range of single-syllable word types — varying vowels, clusters and codas
Apply blending to words containing digraphs once grapheme knowledge is established
Practise blending through word games, oral riddles and chants — building fluent blending as a reading tool
nodes.hinge_reason: Blending fluency is the core decoding mechanism in LY04 and LY12 — students who cannot reliably blend phonemes into words cannot read connected text using phonics, and their decoding will remain halting and inaccurate.

response_modes.reason: Blending fluency is the core decoding mechanism — it must become fast and accurate. Slow or inaccurate blending limits reading. Practice to fluency across word types is required before width adds value.

success_criteria: Student blends three separately spoken phonemes into a recognisable word.
Student can blend words of varying CVC, CVCC and CCVC patterns.

nodes.label: Segmenting: words into sounds
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can segment a single-syllable spoken word into its constituent phonemes — saying each sound separately.
nodes.minimum_width: Segment a CVC word into three phonemes (e.g. 'can' → /c/-/a/-/n/).
nodes.typical_width: Segment single-syllable spoken words into phonemes — including CVC, CVCC and CCVC patterns; say each phoneme distinctly; understand this as the inverse of blending.
wider: Segment words across a wide range of single-syllable types — varying onset, vowel and coda
Apply segmenting to words with digraphs (once grapheme knowledge supports this) — recognising that 'sh' is one phoneme
Connect segmenting to spelling — use segmentation to support encoding in writing tasks
nodes.hinge_reason: Segmenting is the prerequisite for spelling — students who cannot segment a spoken word into phonemes cannot apply letter-sound knowledge to encode it in writing (LY12, LY13). Segmenting errors propagate directly into misspelling.

response_modes.reason: Segmenting is the inverse of blending and equally foundational for spelling. Consistent accuracy across word types is required — errors propagate directly into misspelling.

success_criteria: Student segments a CVC word into three separate phonemes.
Student can segment both onset and rime of a word.

nodes.label: Phoneme manipulation: add, delete, substitute
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can manipulate phonemes in single-syllable words by addition, deletion and substitution — generating new words.
nodes.minimum_width: Substitute the initial phoneme in a given word to make a new word (e.g. 'run' → 'fun').
nodes.typical_width: Manipulate phonemes by addition, deletion and substitution at initial, medial and final positions; generate new words through each manipulation type; understand that changing one phoneme changes the word.
wider: Practise phoneme manipulation across all positions — initial, medial, final — systematically exploring minimal pairs
Apply phoneme manipulation to generate a range of words for a rime family — building awareness of word families as phonemic units
Explore phoneme manipulation through word games, chants and minimal pair comparisons

response_modes.reason: Phoneme substitution and deletion can feel arbitrary without multiple examples — students need to work across initial, medial and final positions, and across addition/deletion/substitution, before the principle that phonemes are independently manipulable is secure.

success_criteria: Student can substitute the initial phoneme to make a new word.
Student can delete the initial phoneme and say what remains.
Student can add a phoneme to generate a new word.
